gd.farmer.title: How to use TerraOrb for Farmers
gd.farmer.intro: TerraOrb is for farmers and farmer organisations in the Dry Zone. It reads NASA satellite data and turns it into plain advice for your village tank. First, find your tank on the home page.
gd.farmer.tank.name: Your tank's water
gd.farmer.tank.what: Shows if your tank has more or less water than usual, as a green, amber or red signal, with rain and heat of past seasons.
gd.farmer.tank.step1: Type your tank's name in the box 'Search tanks', or tap your tank on the map.
gd.farmer.tank.step2: Read the colour and the short sentence at the top of the plan page.
gd.farmer.tank.step3: Press 'See water and rain charts' to see the tank's water and rain over the years.
gd.farmer.tank.step4: Switch from 'Simple' to 'Advanced' if you want to see the numbers and sources.
gd.farmer.tank.tip: Rain and heat come from NASA POWER, and greenness from NASA MODIS. Some tanks show 'Water not checked yet' because the satellite reading is not ready; we never guess.
gd.farmer.advice.name: What to sow now
gd.farmer.advice.what: Lists the crops that suit the rain expected at your tank right now, in plain words.
gd.farmer.advice.step1: Open your tank from the home page.
gd.farmer.advice.step3: Read each crop: good, risky or not now.
gd.farmer.advice.step4: Ask your Agricultural Instructor before you sow.
gd.farmer.advice.tip: The advice compares the expected rain with what each crop needs. The crop numbers are drafts and the rain forecast is not certain.
gd.farmer.week.name: This week's advice
gd.farmer.week.what: A short list of things to do and to watch out for this week at your tank. It is made from the satellite data and the weather forecast.
gd.farmer.week.step1: Open your tank from the home page.
gd.farmer.week.step3: Read the lines marked 'Do this', 'Watch out' and 'Good to know'.
gd.farmer.week.step4: Press 'Share on WhatsApp' or 'Copy the text' to send it to others.
gd.farmer.week.tip: The weather lines come from Open-Meteo, which is not NASA data. They update about every 10 minutes while you are online, and forecasts can change.
gd.farmer.calendar.name: Sowing calendar
gd.farmer.calendar.what: Shows the best weeks to sow each crop over the next 12 weeks, based on expected and usual rain.
gd.farmer.calendar.step3: Choose a crop under 'Choose a crop'.
gd.farmer.calendar.step4: Tap a square to see what that week means.
gd.farmer.calendar.tip: Paddy is watered from the tank, so its bars follow the tank's water. Other crops follow the rain. Rain forecasts are never certain.
gd.farmer.weather.name: Weather and rain map
gd.farmer.weather.what: Shows today's weather, the next 16 days and a map of recent rain from space.
gd.farmer.weather.step1: Open your tank from the home page.
gd.farmer.weather.step3: Tap a day in 'Next 16 days' to see its rain and heat.
gd.farmer.weather.step4: Use the map to see where rain fell recently.
gd.farmer.weather.tip: The 16-day forecast is from Open-Meteo (not NASA data). The map is a NASA satellite picture (GIBS). A forecast can be wrong.
gd.farmer.farm.name: My farm plan
gd.farmer.farm.what: Lets you add your own field, see its land parts and get crop plans with the reasons. It needs a phone number to sign in.
gd.farmer.farm.step1: Open 'My farm plan' in the menu.
gd.farmer.farm.step2: Type your phone number and press 'Send me a code'.
gd.farmer.farm.step3: Type the code and press 'Sign in'.
gd.farmer.farm.step4: Press 'Add a farm', tap your field on the map and save it.
gd.farmer.farm.tip: Your phone number only keeps your farms private to you. Land parts are modelled from terrain data, not measured. This tool supports your Agricultural Instructor; it does not replace them.
